hidden_case.description: The producer's normalizer strips ISO-8601 timestamps, unittest elapsed-duration numbers, and the clone's own absolute path, on the theory that these are the only legitimately non-deterministic fields. I checked whether this list is complete by examining what environment variables double_clone_runner.py actually passes to each `python3 -I -B <test>` subprocess: {LANG, LC_ALL, PATH, TMPDIR}. Notably, unlike the sibling unit po03-wa-b2e7-001-clean-clone-runner's clean_environment() (which explicitly sets PYTHONHASHSEED=0), this runner's run_suite() does NOT set PYTHONHASHSEED at all, and builds a fresh environment dict rather than inheriting the parent's. I constructed a minimal test file that prints a Python set's iteration order (a legitimate, common pattern in diagnostic test output) and ran it twice under the EXACT environment configuration this runner uses (LANG/LC_ALL/PATH set, no PYTHONHASHSEED, no inheritance of a fixed seed).
hidden_case.command: env -i LANG=C.UTF-8 LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 PATH="$PATH" python3 -I -B test_hash_order.py (run twice, no PYTHONHASHSEED set, matching double_clone_runner.py's actual subprocess environment construction)
hidden_case.outcome: CONFIRMS A REAL GAP -- printed set/dict iteration order is genuinely non-deterministic across separate invocations under this runner's actual subprocess environment (Python's default hash randomization is not pinned), and this class of legitimate non-determinism is neither normalized out of the canonical output nor disclosed as a limitation, unlike timestamps/elapsed-time/clone-path which ARE handled.
hidden_case.analysis: This does not invalidate today's PASS verdict, because none of the PO-03 suite's CURRENT committed tests happen to print unordered set/dict content (confirmed: my real-repo run against all 12 current test files produced byte_equivalent=true with zero unexpected diffs). But it is a genuine, demonstrable latent defect in the general mechanism the falsifiable hypothesis claims ('two independent clean clones ... produce byte-identical canonical outputs'): if any current or future PO-03 test ever prints hash-order-sensitive content, this runner would either (a) falsely report byte_equivalent=false for two functionally identical clones (a false-negative undermining trust in the tool), or worse (b) coincidentally happen to match on a given pair of runs and give a false sense of security. The sibling unit 001 in this same cohort already solved this exact problem by pinning PYTHONHASHSEED=0; this unit's independently-written environment-construction code did not carry that fix over.
